gaps: No platform (DoorDash, Uber, Grubhub) discloses courier headcount at state, county, metro or city level; no 'X Dashers in Los Angeles' or 'X in San Francisco' figure exists in official filings or impact reports found.

Official counts are 'ever-active in the year' (DoorDash 'people who dashed', Uber 'monthly active drivers and couriers'); the only official intensity stat is DoorDash's ~4 hours/week average (Q4 2025). No official daily-active or full-time-equivalent courier count exists, so daily-active rider counts for DTLA+Koreatown cannot be read off any platform disclosure.
Uber reports drivers and couriers as one combined number; no Eats-only courier count, no US/CA split, no vehicle-mode share.

DoorDash publishes per-city two-wheeled shares only for a handful of cities (DC, Philadelphia, Boston, Toronto in the Feb-2025 report; SF and Seattle in a 2026 edition per snippet). Los Angeles is absent from every DoorDash two-wheel city list found, so LA's official two-wheel share is unknown.

No platform breaks 'two-wheeled' down into bicycle vs e-bike vs e-scooter vs moped vs motorcycle, and no platform publishes a car / two-wheel / walking split for LA. The task-1 vehicle-mode split cannot come from official platform data alone.
Grubhub's 200,000-courier figure is undated and pre-Wonder; Grubhub now has no public filings.
Platform order volumes are global/consolidated; no LA or SF order counts are disclosed (only a qualitative metro ranking placing greater LA first).
The 2026 DoorDash Two-Wheeled Progress Report URL was not located within budget; the SF 72% figure is snippet-only and must be verified.

Platform vehicle-class eligibility for 40-70 mph e-mopeds/e-motorcycles (HMP FLASH, Lightning MK.II) is unclear: Uber's public scooter rule is '<50cc'; whether these register as 'motorcycle' or 'car' class on DoorDash/Uber Eats, and whether that affects order allocation, is not documented in sources found.
must_ask_hmp: Platform mix of HMP's SF customers (DoorDash / Uber Eats / Grubhub / Amazon Flex / other) and share who multi-app - no public source gives this.

Self-reported working intensity of HMP customers: days per week, hours per day, orders per day, monthly gross earnings by vehicle class (needed to convert platform 'ever-active' counts into daily-active professional riders).

How HMP customers register their FLASH / Lightning MK.II / SWFT MAXX on each platform (bike, scooter, motorcycle, car dash type) and whether any have been deactivated or restricted for vehicle class - determines which platform vehicle category the LA fleet should target.
Whether HMP has any existing contact or partnership discussion with DoorDash (Dasher perks / two-wheel program, like the Whizz-Chicago and Swobbee-NYC deals) or Uber Eats courier programs.
Home and working zip codes / neighborhoods of the >1,000 SF vehicle owners and ~300 battery renters, to define the SF core-zone benchmark denominator.
Any HMP customer who already works in LA or has relocated from SF to LA, and any inbound LA inquiries by month (demand signal no platform data can provide).
surprises: DoorDash's San Francisco two-wheeled delivery share is reported at 72% (2026 report, snippet-only; DC was 57% in the 2025 report). SF is one of the most two-wheel-heavy DoorDash markets in North America, which means the SF benchmark may overstate what LA (absent from all DoorDash two-wheel city lists) will deliver.
DoorDash states two-wheeled Dashers earn ~10% more than car Dashers in the top 20 delivery cities - an official talking point HMP can cite to riders.

DoorDash's average Dasher works only ~4 hours/week (Q4 2025) and 85% have other income; the 8-9 million Dasher headline is therefore an extremely loose upper bound on professional couriers, reinforcing the CONTEXT's warning against single-ratio estimates.

Uber Eats' public scooter requirement is an engine 'below 50cc'; HMP's 40-70 mph e-moped/e-motorcycle products may fall outside Uber's 'scooter' class, which could affect LA fleet-mix and platform eligibility assumptions.

DoorDash already channels Dashers to competitors' services: an official Whizz e-bike rental partnership (Chicago, $9 first month) and a Swobbee battery-swap discount (NYC) - the platform itself is a distribution channel for rental/swap providers, relevant to the Whizz/Zoomo competitor task.
The search summary ranks greater Los Angeles first among DoorDash metros by order volume (ahead of NY metro and SF Bay Area), supporting LA demand scale even though no LA Dasher count exists.
